'''Erich Hans Rothe''' (July 21, 1895, [[Berlin]] – February 19, 1988, [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]) was a German-born American mathematician, who did research in [[mathematical analysis]], [[differential equation]]s, [[integral equation]]s, and [[mathematical physics]].<ref name=macbio>{{MacTutor Biography|title=Erich Hans Rothe|id=Rothe_Erich}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Displaced German Scholars: A Guide to Academics in Peril in Nazi Germany During the 1930s|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=47XdGC6Ch-wC&pg=PA53|date=1 January 1993|publisher=Wildside Press LLC|page=53|isbn=978-0-89370-474-2}}</ref> He is known for the Rothe method (also known as the method of lines or the method of semidiscretization) used for solving [[evolution equation]]s.<ref name="Rothe1930">{{cite journal|last1=Rothe|first1=Erich|title=Zweidimensionale parabolische Randwertaufgaben als Grenzfall eindimensionaler Randwertaufgaben|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=102|issue=1|year=1930|pages=650–670|issn=0025-5831|doi=10.1007/BF01782368|s2cid=123325520 }}</ref><ref name="Kačur1986">{{cite book|chapter=''Method of Rothe in evolution equations'' by J. Kačur|volume=1192|year=1986|pages=23–34|issn=0075-8434|title=Equadiff 6: Proceedings of the International Conference on Differential Equations and their Applications, held in Brno, Czechoslovakia August 21–30, 1985|doi=10.1007/BFb0076049|hdl=10338.dmlcz/700142 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Rothe, whose father was a lawyer, attended Berlin's [[Royal Wilhelm Gymnasium]] and passed his ''[[Abitur]]'' in October 1913. After completing two semesters at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], he volunteered to join the German Army in a field artillery regiment. He was wounded in the [[Battle of Verdun]] and was discharged from the German Army in December 1918. In 1919, he continued his mathematical studies for one semester at [[Technische Hochschule Berlin]] and then transferred to the [[Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin]]. There he studied mathematics, physics, and philosophy and in 1923 passed the ''Lehramtsexamen'' qualifying him to become a ''[[Gymnasium (Germany)|Gymnasium]]'' teacher. From 1923 to 1926, he taught at Berlin's ''Mommsen-Gymnasium''.<ref name=macbio/> In 1927, he received his [[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']] from Technische Hochschule Berlin. His dissertation ''Über einige Analogien zwischen linearen partiellen und linearen gewöhnlichen Differentialgleichungen'' (About some analogies between linear partial and linear ordinary differential equations) was supervised by [[Erhard Schmidt]] and [[Richard von Mises]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|name=Erich Hans Rothe|id=7784}}</ref> Rothe worked from 1926 to 1927 at the Institute of Applied Mathematics of the Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin. In 1928, he married the mathematician [[Hildegard Rothe-Ille|Hildegard Ille]] (1899–1942).<ref name=macbio/> From 1928 to 1931, he was a ''[[Privatdozent]]'' and ''Assistent'' under [[Fritz Noether]] at the ''[[Technische Hochschule Breslau]]''. There he received his ''[[Habilitation]]'' in 1928. From 1931 to 1935, he was a ''Privatdozent'' at the [[University of Breslau]]. There he received his ''Umhabilitation'' in 1931).<ref>{{cite book|editor=Scharlau, Winfried|editor-link=Winfried Scharlau|title=Mathematische Institute in Deutschland, 1800–1945|publisher=Vieweg|year=1990|pages=64 & 70|doi=10.1007/978-3-663-14036-8 |isbn=978-3-528-08992-4 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007%2F978-3-663-14036-8}}</ref><ref>The term ''Umhabilitation'' refers to the academic procedure in which [[professors]] or ''[[Privatdozent]]en'' acquire the license to teach (''[[venia legendi]]'') at another university by means of a shortened procedure.</ref> During the time he held positions in Breslau, he took study leave for a year at the [[University of Göttingen]]. In Breslau in April 1931, Hildegard Rothe gave birth to Erhard W. Rothe.<ref name=macbio/>

After being dismissed in 1935 from the German civil service because he was a Jew, Rothe with his wife and son escaped to Zurich and emigrated in 1937 to the USA. From 1937 to 1943, he taught mathematics (with a very small salary) at [[William Penn College]] in [[Oskaloosa, Iowa]].<ref name=macbio/><ref name="Siegmund-Schultze2009">{{cite book|author=Siegmund-Schultze, Reinhard|title=Mathematicians Fleeing from Nazi Germany: Individual Fates and Global Impact|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jBoEmGB3B3MC&pg=194|page=194|year=2009|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-12593-0}}</ref> His wife died of cancer in December 1942. At the [[University of Michigan]], Rothe was an assistant professor from 1944 to 1949, an associate professor from 1949 to 1955, and a full professor from 1955 to 1964, when he retired as professor emeritus.<ref name=macbio/> In retirement, he taught at the [[University of Michigan–Dearborn]]<ref name=FHP>{{cite web|title=Erich Hans Rothe|website=Faculty History Project, University of Michigan|url=http://faculty-history.dc.umich.edu/faculty/erich-hans-rothe|access-date=2025-02-25|archive-date=2021-05-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515204859/http://faculty-history.dc.umich.edu/faculty/erich-hans-rothe|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in the academic year from 1967 to 1968 at [[Western Michigan University]] (WMU).<ref name=macbio/> During his year at WMU, Rothe helped to develop the PhD program for WMU's mathematics department, which awarded its first PhD in December 1969.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Brief History of Mathematics at WMU|journal=Mathematical Association of America Michigan Section Newsletter|date=December 2003|volume=30|issue=1|page=16|url=http://sections.maa.org/michigan/newsletters/30_1%20Fall%202003%20Newsletter.pdf}}</ref>

Rothe published more than 50 mathematical papers.<ref name=FHP/> He was a co-author, with [[Hans Rademacher]], of chapter 19 of the 7th edition of ''Die Differential- und Integralgleichungen der Mechanik und Physik''.<ref>{{cite book|editor=von Mises, Richard|editor2=Frank, Philipp|title=Die Differential- und Integralgleichungen der Mechanik und Physik: als 7. Auflage von Riemann-Webers Partiellen Differentialgleichungen der mathematischen Physik|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wjvvAAAAMAAJ&q=rothe|year=1925|publisher=F. Vieweg}}</ref> In 1986 at the age of 91, Rothe published the 242-page book ''Introduction to Various Aspects of Degree Theory in Banach Spaces''.<ref name=macbio/>

In addition to the Rothe Method, he is also known for his theorem, proven in 1937, that a functional in a [[Hilbert space]] is weakly continuous if and only if its [[Fréchet derivative]] is a [[Compact operator#Completely continuous operators|completely continuous operator]]<ref>{{cite journal|author=Cesari, Lamberto|title=Introductory remarks to a lecture of Erich H. Rothe|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|volume=12|year=1965|issue=3 |pages=382–383|doi=10.1016/0022-247X(65)90003-X |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82624044.pdf}}</ref><ref>Maximilian Pinl: ''Kollegen in einer dunklen Zeit'', Jahresbericht der DMV '''71''', 208/209, 1969</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Rothe, E. H.|title=Über Abbildungsklassen von Kugeln des Hilbertschen Raumes|journal=Compositio Math.|volume=4|year=1937|pages=294–307}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Rothe, E. H.|title=Über den Abbildungsgrad bei Abbildungen von Kugeln des Hilbertschen Raumes|journal=Compositio Math.|volume=5|year=1937|pages=166–176}}</ref> and for Rothe's fixed point theorem, proven in 1937.<ref name="Smart1980">{{cite book|author=Smart, D. R.|title=Fixed Point Theorems|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=y5g4AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA26|pages=26–27|date=14 February 1980|publisher=CUP Archive|isbn=978-0-521-29833-9}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Rothe, E. H.|title=Zur Theorie der topologischen Ordnung und der Vektorfelder in Benachschen Raumen|journal=Compositio Math.|volume=5|year=1937|pages=177–197}}</ref> In 1978 a collection of papers was published in his honor.<ref name="Rothe1978">{{cite book|editor=Cesari, L.|editor2=Kannan, R.|editor3=Weinberger, H. F.|title=Nonlinear Analysis: A Collection of Papers in Honor of Erich H. Rothe|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OC7vAAAAMAAJ|year=1978|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-165550-1}} (This book contains a list of Rothe's publications.)</ref> His doctoral students include [[Jane Cronin Scanlon]] and [[George J. Minty]].<ref name=Kaplan>{{cite journal|author=Kaplan, Wilfred|title=A tribute to Erich H. Rothe|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|volume=12|issue=3|year=1965|pages=381–382|doi=10.1016/0022-247X(65)90002-8 |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/81151477.pdf}}</ref>

Upon his death, Erich Rothe was survived by his son and two granddaughters.<ref name=FHP/>
